miniProject.title: Validate a bounded extension and defend its evidence
miniProject.brief: Use `loglab` to validate one bounded real-code extension, preserving the working data path as a reference fallback. Connect finite models, replayable failure histories and repeated measurements to a reproduction package that separates checked guarantees from assumptions and local evidence on your machine.
steps: Pin the real-system component you will extend and trace protocol, storage, replication, consistency, recovery, security and operations paths against code and documentation. Retain control-plane/data-plane state ownership, extracted contracts and ML provenance closure; contrast quorum and CRDT dissemination assumptions using the earlier convergence proof.

Run TLC on the pinned TLA+ Examples TwoPhase specification, then model your `loglab` log in `spec/` with explicit environment actions and a refinement mapping. Check committed-prefix safety and conditional liveness; retain bounds, boundary behavior, fairness assumptions, state counts and each extension's first meaningful counterexample.

Extend the deterministic scheduler in `net/` and `faults/` with explicit persistence completions and crash/restart state separation. Use Hypothesis stateful tests against an independent model; plant a recovery or ownership bug, retain its shrunk program and schedule, replay independently of random draws, and state uncontrolled nondeterminism.

Build generator, client, nemesis and checker roles around a fault/workload matrix in `history/`. Validate normalization of pending, ambiguous and retried operations against fixed histories using Knossos register and Elle read-write-register checks; retain scoped verdicts, empty coverage cells and minimized safety and bounded non-progress histories.

Implement the proposed bounded component change through `loglab`, retaining the reference fallback. Check unit, property, integration and fault layers independently against baseline contracts before timing; retain failing-then-passing regressions, old-data and mixed-version migration tests, rollback drills, and ambiguous-outcome reconciliation with preserved request identity.

Predeclare three mechanism-isolating ablations across three bottleneck-distinct workload regions in `bench/`. After correctness gates pass, repeat matched baseline, extension and fallback runs with named versions and workloads; retain raw latency, goodput, resource, checkpoint and recovery records, uncertainty and an honest neutral or negative result.

Package raw message, state, WAL and processor histories, pinned environment manifest, seeds, schedules, configurations and per-claim commands in `reports/` for independent reproduction. Label claims proved, model-checked within bounds, simulated, locally measured or inferred; quantitatively defend three architectures across workload, failure, consistency, cost and evolution.
deliverables: Architecture reconstruction, contracts, provenance closure, bounded log specifications and retained TLC counterexamples in `spec/` and `reports/`.
The bounded real-code patch, reference fallback, migration and rollback evidence, layered tests and replayable minimized failures.
Ablation records, workload-region comparisons and the preserved negative result with versions, raw measurements and uncertainty.
An independently exercised reproduction package and evidence-labeled defense comparing simpler architectures and cross-region assumptions.

checks.name: TLA+ Examples: TwoPhase with TLC
checks.note: Keep public-model results separate from your log model; neither a safety-only specification nor a finite run proves implementation liveness.

checks.name: Hypothesis stateful crash and restart tests
checks.note: Retain the pinned testing version, planted-bug failure, shrunk program and reference-model assertions; generated executions do not exhaust all interleavings.

checks.name: Knossos single-register history checks
checks.note: Calibrate on fixed histories and retain the dependency version; do not extend a register verdict to unmodeled objects or transactions.

checks.name: Elle read-write-register history checks
checks.note: Use the section's model-specific API and pinned runtime; report supported anomalies, history completeness and indeterminate outcomes beside each verdict.

rubric.pass: Your bounded TLC model checks committed-prefix safety with explicit environment and fairness assumptions. Reference-model property tests catch the planted recovery bug and replay its shrunk schedule.
rubric.strong: A trace-to-model mapping exposes a missing action or abstraction mismatch; the corrected model and code retain separate regression evidence without claiming a general proof.

rubric.pass: Your normalizer preserves ambiguity and incarnations; Knossos and Elle agree with fixed-history oracles within their scopes. The campaign retains checker verdicts and minimized safety and conditional non-progress examples.
rubric.strong: A negative-control checker or normalization defect changes a verdict, and its regression identifies the observation lost rather than merely repairing event formatting.

rubric.pass: Your code-and-documentation reconstruction identifies state and contracts. Independently failing test layers verify the bounded change, fallback, old data, mixed versions, migration, rollback and retry identity after ambiguity.
rubric.strong: Faults during fallback activation and rollback preserve ownership, effect and durability contracts; provenance identifies which derived artifacts require invalidation or rebuild.

rubric.pass: An independent reader reproduces exact checks from the package. Repeated matched comparisons retain three ablations, three regions, uncertainty and a negative result; three architectures receive quantitative, evidence-labeled comparisons.
rubric.strong: The defense separates measured behavior from inferred geo-replication and disaggregation costs, identifies unsupported claims, and uses the retained alternatives to justify removing an unhelpful mechanism.

miniProject.feedsInto: The bounded real-code extension, formal and property checks, minimized failures, ablations and independently exercised reproduction package complete the capstone dossier; contracts and regressions also strengthen every earlier `loglab` subsystem.
